newsitem.title: GERMANY: German VDA sees car registrations rising in 1997.
newsitem.headline: German VDA sees car registrations rising in 1997.

text.p: The German automobile association (VDA) said on Wednesday that it expects German car production, registrations and exports to grow by two to three percent this year.
The group also said that investment in the German car sector was expected to rise by five percent this year and that employment in the sector would stabilise.
The group said that 1997 domestic car registrations could rise by three percent to 3.6 million units.
VDA president Bernd Gottschalk made the remarks in a speech at the association's annual press conference.
He said Germany's share of the global car market climbed to 14.7 percent in 1996 from 14.2 percent the year before.
But foreign car markets face difficulties and will grow more slowly, or even shrink in 1997.
